slides.title: From Acceleration Back to Position
slides.lede: Opener: two scenes, six questions and a recap, answered on your boards

slides.title: Two Cars, One Push
slides.alt: Two toy cars in two lanes, drawn large

slides.eyebrow: Two cars, one push · The situation
slides.title: One acceleration, two cars

setup.preamble: Two toy cars sit side by side at the origin $O$. They get exactly the same push: the same acceleration. The lanes show the cars, and the graphs below show $a$, $v$ and $s$ against $t$.
setup.para: Both cars are at $O$ at $t=0$. Car A starts from rest, and car B starts with a velocity of $3\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Both have an acceleration of $a=2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ for $0\le t\le 4$ seconds, so there is only one $a$-$t$ graph. The area under each graph is shaded as time runs.

facts.html: Both cars start at $O$, so $s=0$ at $t=0$
Car A starts from rest: $v=0$ at $t=0$
Car B starts at $v=3\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ at $t=0$
Both have the same $a=2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, for $0\le t\le 4$ seconds

scene.alt: Two toy cars in two lanes above one number line, over the graphs of acceleration, velocity and position against time, with the areas shaded as time runs

slides.title: Who gains more velocity?
slides.stem: Both cars feel the same acceleration for $4$ seconds. Which car gains more velocity?

walk.cap: The shaded area is a rectangle
walk.note: The area under the $a$-$t$ graph is the change in velocity.

scene.alt: Two toy cars in two lanes above one number line, over the graphs of acceleration, velocity and position against time, with the areas shaded as time runs

choices: Car A, which starts from rest
Car B, which is already moving

slides.title: Which car is ahead?
slides.stem: Both cars start at $O$. Now watch the two velocities. At $t=4$, which car is ahead, and by how much?

walk.cap: The area under each velocity graph

walk.note: Car B is $12$ m ahead: the extra $3\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ for $4$ s is the rectangle $3\times 4=12$.

scene.alt: Two toy cars in two lanes above one number line, over the graphs of acceleration, velocity and position against time, with the areas shaded as time runs

slides.title: A third car
slides.stem: Car C has the same acceleration and the same starting velocity as car B, but it starts $5$ m to the right of $O$. Where is car C at $t=4$?

walk.note: Car C has the same $v$-$t$ graph as car B, so it travels the same $28$ m.
The area only tells us how far the car moves. We also need to know where it started.

scene.alt: Two toy cars in two lanes above one number line, over the graphs of acceleration, velocity and position against time, with the areas shaded as time runs

slides.title: The Fading Push
slides.alt: A toy car on a number line, drawn large

setup.preamble: This toy car starts from rest at $O$. This time the push fades away: the acceleration gets smaller as time goes on, but it never quite reaches zero.
setup.para: At $t=0$ the car is at $O$ and at rest. Its acceleration is $a(t)=2e^{-0.5t}$ metres per second squared, for $0\le t\le 12$ seconds. The area under the $a$-$t$ graph is shaded as time runs.

facts.html: At $O$ and at rest: $s=0$ and $v=0$ at $t=0$
Acceleration $a(t)=2e^{-0.5t}$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$, for $0\le t\le 12$ seconds
The acceleration is always positive, but it gets smaller

scene.alt: A toy car on a number line above the graphs of acceleration, velocity and position against time, with the areas shaded as time runs

slides.title: After a long time
slides.stem: The acceleration is always positive. After a long time, what happens to the velocity?

walk.note: Each second adds a smaller area than the one before.

walk.cap: The velocity rises, then levels off

scene.alt: A toy car on a number line above the graphs of acceleration, velocity and position against time, with the areas shaded as time runs

choices: It keeps growing without any limit
It rises, then falls back to zero

slides.title: Heading for what value?
slides.stem: At $t=12$ the velocity is about $3.99\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and still rising. What value is it heading towards?

walk.note: The area under $2e^{-0.5t}$ from $0$ to $t$ is the velocity, because $v(0)=0$.
This is the limiting velocity: the velocity gets close to $4$ but never reaches it.

scene.alt: A toy car on a number line above the graphs of acceleration, velocity and position against time, with the areas shaded as time runs

slides.title: How far by 12 seconds?
slides.stem: If the car had travelled at exactly $4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ for all $12$ seconds, it would have gone $48$ m. How far has the real car gone?

walk.cap: The area under the velocity graph
walk.note: The slow start costs the car about $8$ m.

scene.alt: A toy car on a number line above the graphs of acceleration, velocity and position against time, with the areas shaded as time runs

cards: A larger $a$ tilts the $v$-$t$ graph more.
A different start lifts the $v$-$t$ graph.
$a$ and the start decide the motion.
